requirement: Submit an annual report no later than March 1 summarizing the DSM plan and total actual achieved results for the preceding calendar year.

For each approved program: the name of the utility.
The name of the program and program start date.
The calendar year the report covers.
The total number of customers, or other appropriate unit of measure, by customer class for each calendar year of the planning horizon.
The total number of customers eligible to participate in the program for each calendar year of the planning horizon.
The total number of customers projected to participate in the program for each calendar year of the planning horizon.
The potential cumulative penetration level to date: projected participating customers to date as a percentage of total eligible customers in the class.
The actual number of program participants and the current cumulative number of program participants.
The actual cumulative penetration level: actual cumulative participants as a percentage of eligible customers in the class.
A comparison of the actual cumulative penetration level to the potential cumulative penetration level.
A justification for any variance greater than 15% from the annual goals established by the Commission.
Annual KWH, winter KW and summer KW reductions, at the meter and the generation level, per installation and program total.
The per installation cost and the total program cost of the utility.
The net benefits for measures installed during the reporting period, annualized over the life of the program (annual benefits = Bnpv x d / [1 - (1+d)^-n]).
The goals the report compares against are the annual goals the Commission set in the utility's 2024 goals order.

An annual final true-up showing the common costs, individual program costs and revenues, and actual total ECCR revenues for the most recent 12-month historical period, with a comparison to the costs and revenues previously estimated.
A list of the account and subaccount numbers used for ECCR.
All data sources and calculations used to substantiate claims of potential energy savings included in advertisements.
